question: Does a fresh 900-second admission window produce a useful cross-job route reply after discovery?
baseline: 2026-10-25 business-client run, exact initial files/messages/plan/fixtures reused
intervention: Actor admission 300 to 900 seconds; run admission 600 to 1200 seconds; all other runtime, task and model/provider settings retained
persistence: Same context within this fresh run; never resume or replay the earlier run
primary: Independently grounded request-read-reply-read-source-use chain; cross-job replies exclude own-note followups
secondary: Client discovery/execution, model-visible foreign notes/cards, exact note graph, full reciprocal closure, 8 reviews, response cost and admission end reasons
comparison_limit: One exploratory run per window on different dates and credentials; not a causal or population-rate estimate
unknown_policy: No retries, fallback or replay; unknown requests hold this study; already admitted streams settle without interruption
preservation: New one-shot namespace, incremental durable frames/responses/tools and exact source copies, hash-verified local backup; old runs remain read-only
execution: Unchanged native Docker v3 collector with a source-validation adapter, not generic Harbor model execution
